question.problem: Find the set of values of $w$ that satisfy $w-3\le -1$ or $5w>25.$ Express your answer in interval notation.
question.worked_solution:
We start by solving $w-3\le -1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}w-3+3 & \le -1+3 \\ w & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/41894afbf397505568367e80d14e34fe2b04a2acdfd5398bd8ba41727b8c67c6.png)

Then, we solve $5w>25:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5w}{5} & >\frac{25}{5} \\ w & >5\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/262a3e683cb8c8a67cdd58c0f138e44466c346092c7f74ec03ec1483a385056a.png)

To graph the values of $w$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/95d67331522c16093207de451a33bb713b42e1418d1f4c1a7aa1ef6369a51e4b.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $w\le 2$ or $w>5.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-\infty ,2]\cup (5,\infty ).
$$
